title: Twill or plain weave: how to tell the weave
notes: English test video T1 (restart 03.11.2026): same scenes, photos, Kling clips and sound cues as the German T1; text from the EN pilot (menswear-20261202-3-en.P1), translated, not rewritten; Gemini voice Algenib (Flash). AI images show appearance, never the weave; twill images mirrored so the twill line runs from top right to bottom left (Woolmark p. 9).

layout.description: Two dark suit fabrics, same colour, and yet woven differently: plain weave or twill. Drawn thread by thread: how warp and weft cross, why a twill has a diagonal line and how to tell the weave on your own jacket. Illustration, source: Woolmark, Introduction to Wovenwear.
layout.companion_text: Suitwerk shows menswear in detail, drawn rather than claimed. No advertising, no product recommendations.

beats.spoken: Two suit fabrics, same colour, same wool. And yet they are woven differently. Only a linen tester shows you the difference.

data.source: Woolmark: Introduction to Wovenwear, p. 9 · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: Fabric A is a plain weave. The lengthwise threads are the warp, the crosswise thread is the weft. It goes over one warp thread, then under the next, always alternating. The next weft does the exact opposite. That is the simplest weave.

data.title: Plain weave
data.colors_note: Colours only to tell them apart
data.source: Woolmark: Introduction to Wovenwear, p. 9 · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: Fabric B is a twill. Here the weft goes over two warp threads and under two. Each new weft moves along by one thread. That creates a diagonal line, the twill line.

data.title: Twill
data.colors_note: Colours only to tell them apart
data.source: Woolmark: Introduction to Wovenwear, p. 9 · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: On squared paper, thread by thread: Each dark square here means: warp on top. The plain weave becomes a chessboard, the twill a staircase.

data.source: Drawn after Woolmark: Introduction to Wovenwear, p. 9

beats.spoken: Now turn both fabrics over. The plain weave looks the same on both sides. The twill has a face: there the line usually runs from top right to bottom left.

data.source: Woolmark: Introduction to Wovenwear, p. 9 · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: Both are genuine suit fabrics. For worsted suits, Woolmark lists plain weaves, twills and gabardines. Hold your sleeve at an angle to the light: if you see fine diagonals, it is a twill. Follow Suitwerk for menswear with an eye for detail.
